notes.meaning: The people of Jerusalem chose Ahaziah, the youngest son of Jehoram, to be their new king. Raiders who came with the Arabs had attacked the camp and killed all of his older brothers. Because he was the only surviving heir, the throne of Judah rightfully passed to him.

Ahaziah took the throne and ruled in Jerusalem for only one year. His mother was Athaliah, the granddaughter of King Omri of Israel, who brought northern idol worship into Judah. Although some Hebrew copies say forty-two, ancient translations say he was twenty-two years old, which fits the record since his father died at age forty.

Ahaziah followed the sinful ways of King Ahab's household in Israel instead of honoring the Lord. His mother Athaliah gave him evil advice and pushed him to worship false gods. Her influence made him act more like a son of Ahab than a descendant of David.

Ahaziah did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, just as the family of Ahab had done. After his father died, Ahab's relatives served as his royal advisers and led him straight toward ruin. Listening to wicked advice corrupts a leader and brings destruction.

Following the advice of his ungodly counselors, Ahaziah joined King Joram of Israel to fight against King Hazael of Aram at Ramoth-gilead. He repeated the exact mistake of an ungodly alliance that his grandfather had made years before. In the battle, the Aramean army wounded Joram.

King Joram retreated to the city of Jezreel to recover from the battle wounds he received from the Arameans. Ahaziah then traveled north from his own kingdom to Jezreel to visit his wounded uncle and ally. What seemed like a friendly family visit placed Ahaziah right in the path of danger.

Ahaziah's visit was planned by God to bring about the king's downfall as judgment for his sin. When Ahaziah arrived in Jezreel, he rode out with Joram to meet Jehu. God had already chosen and anointed Jehu to wipe out the evil family of Ahab.

While Jehu was carrying out God's judgment against the household of Ahab, he encountered leaders from Judah and nephews of Ahaziah who served the king. Because they were closely tied to Ahab's wicked court, Jehu put them all to death. Keeping company with the ungodly brought them into the same destruction.

Jehu's men searched for Ahaziah, captured him while he was hiding in Samaria, and put him to death. The soldiers gave him a respectful burial only out of honor for his godly grandfather Jehoshaphat, who had sought the Lord with all his heart. With Ahaziah dead and his relatives slain, no one in his house was left strong enough to rule.

When Athaliah learned that her son Ahaziah had died, she attempted to murder all the remaining royal heirs of Judah. She sought to destroy the house of David completely so she could seize the throne and rule the nation herself. Her bloody plan seemed to threaten the very family line through which God had promised the Messiah would come.

Princess Jehoshabeath secretly rescued Ahaziah's baby son Joash while the other royal children were being murdered. She hid the infant and his nurse inside a bedroom where bedding was kept. Because she was Ahaziah's sister and the wife of the high priest Jehoiada, she was able to keep the child safe from Athaliah.

Baby Joash remained secretly hidden with the priest's family in the house of the Lord for six years. During those years, the wicked Athaliah ruled over the land of Judah. Even while evil seemed to triumph, God quietly protected the one true heir to David's throne.
